newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Sluggish '97 first half GDP growth seen for Brazil.
newsitem.headline: Sluggish '97 first half GDP growth seen for Brazil.

text.p: The Brazilian economy is expected to grow sluggishly in the 1997 first half as trade and fiscal deficits are likely to keep the government's monetary policy tight, Caspian Securities said in a report.
It also said Brazil's economy would post modest growth of 4.2 percent for all of 1997, most of it concentrated in the second half.
On stocks, Caspian said events rather than economic fundamentals would drive the market in 1997.

Market performance would be affected by such key events as regulatory reform in the telecommunications, electric, oil and gas sectors; falling interest rates; and the privatization of cellular service and giant miner Vale do Rio Doce, it said.
The approval of a constitutional amendment allowing President Fernando Henrique Cardoso to stand for a second term in 1998 would boost stock prices, it added.
Caspian elected as its favorite stocks Telerj, Telebras, Celesc, Cataguazes and Petrobras.

It said the Brazilian stock market, currently traded at an estimated 1997 price-earnings ratio of 9.2, is still cheap after this year'strong gains. It expects a 30 percent U.S. dollar return over the next 13 months.
"Our forecast is based on real earnings growth of 24 percent next year and a gradual expansion of the market's multiple as real interest rates decline in the second half of 1997," it said.

Caspian also said Brazilian stocks will be increasingly dependent on foreign capital inflows in 1997 due to the privatization process, which will significantly increase the supply of primary offerings.
"The flow of funds into the Brazilian equity market must increase by at least two-fold in order to absorb the additional supply of shares," it added.
